workItems.title: R1: contain existing friction and make continuation ambient
workItems.description: Stop existing Voila machinery from interrupting ordinary development while the operational loop is built. Evidence staleness becomes expected during active development (one quiet ambient indicator; no instruction to refresh claims; doctor stops treating ordinary staleness as structural failure). Orientation freshness moves from git-HEAD-only to relevant-content freshness, with HEAD retained as provenance. Verification grouping is prepared so one identical command can serve every applicable claim. The focus capsule is injected before every meaningful Steward turn. Narrow scope: correct the specific READY-to-complete inconsistency; do not build a universal gate-policy system.
acceptanceCriteria: In a fresh Pi session the user says only 'Continue.' and the Steward identifies the correct work and begins useful action without asking for a recap or requiring state maintenance
A commit that changes no orientation-relevant content does not mark orientation stale

Voila deterministically identifies and groups claims with equivalent verification contracts, reports the unique contract count, and exposes a stable integration seam for later shared execution. R1 does not execute each group once or distribute a shared execution result across claims; execution deduplication remains R6 scope.
A work item does not display READY to complete while a known required human or authenticated activity remains pending

The focus capsule injected before a Steward turn contains the accepted objective, active work item, current slice, relevant decisions and non-goals, known blocker, next justified action, and active workers and terminals -- and not the entire ledger

workItems.title: R2: one supervised background operation
workItems.description: Let the Steward launch and supervise one long-running local process without blocking the parent conversation. Operations: start, list, inspect, read output, stop, wait. Structured executable and args only -- no shell string execution. Each process records an operation ID, associated work item, executable and args, working directory, owner, start time, status, exit result, bounded output, and settlement result. Non-goals: remote processes, persistence across machine restart, arbitrary shell sessions, terminal multiplexing, concurrency beyond what proves the loop.
acceptanceCriteria: The Steward launches a test process, continues useful parent work while it runs, receives the result automatically without the developer checking, and acts on the outcome

The ordinary Pi surface shows an authoritative active-operation indicator while an owned operation runs, and the Steward Console shows the operation, its elapsed time, and the work item recorded as its owner
A process result is delivered as one completion event and is never injected into an active stream

workItems.title: R3: one bounded read-only Pi child worker
workItems.description: Let the Steward delegate one useful task to another Pi session and integrate the result without developer coordination. Operations: spawn, inspect, wait, steer, cancel, receive result. Concurrency begins at one. Read-only mode is the v1 default (repository scouting, architecture review, test review, debugging analysis, dependency research, adversarial review). Isolated-write workers come only after the read-only loop is reliable, in a dedicated worktree with explicit path scope, with the parent Steward still responsible for integration. Every assignment carries the project objective, active work item, bounded task, relevant decisions and constraints, permitted scope, expected result, known uncertainty, and return format -- never the full project history.
acceptanceCriteria: The Steward identifies a task worth delegating, creates a bounded assignment, continues parent work, receives the result automatically, evaluates it, integrates or rejects it, and proceeds without asking the developer to carry the result
The developer can inspect the worker transcript, steer it, cancel it, and take over -- as escape hatches, not as normal management requirements
Delegation does not add more elapsed time or coordination than doing the work directly

workItems.title: R4: operational integration and automatic settlement
workItems.description: Turn terminals, workers, project state, and the parent Steward into one coherent loop via the smallest durable representation of active work (operation ID, type, work item, assignment, status, owner, model or executable, working directory or worktree, started and settled times, result summary, artifact references). Explicitly avoid a generalized workflow DSL. Includes drift correction (remind, request justification, cancel if necessary, preserve partial results, escalate only a material plan decision) and failure recovery (inspect, decide on retry, reduce or revise the assignment, switch execution path, continue unaffected work, escalate only a real blocker).
acceptanceCriteria: The loop delegate -> observe -> settle -> evaluate -> integrate -> continue completes without developer orchestration
The Steward avoids issuing a duplicate assignment for work already active
A worker that moves outside its assignment is corrected or cancelled with useful partial results preserved, and the developer is involved only when the drift exposes a material plan decision
A failed worker or process is inspected and handled without escalating anything that is not a real blocker

workItems.title: R5: fresh-session continuity
workItems.description: Make the Steward resilient across context compaction, exit, restart, and a genuinely fresh session, via a persisted continuation record: accepted objective, active work item, current slice, completed actions, changed files, commands and actual results, active or interrupted operations, worker findings, unresolved decisions, failures, and the exact next action. On startup a live process may be reattached when reliable, a dead process previously marked running becomes interrupted, and an abandoned child session is marked honestly.
acceptanceCriteria: A real session is closed mid-work, a new session starts, and 'Continue.' resumes the correct work with no user reconstruction
The Steward reconciles repository state and active or abandoned operations on resume without asking the user to explain what happened
No interrupted operation is silently assumed successful

workItems.title: R6: quiet boundary reconciliation
workItems.description: Preserve evidence honesty while removing the verification treadmill. Reconciliation triggers automatically when a slice appears finished, when completion is requested, when delivery is requested, or when the developer asks for evidence -- not after every source edit. The Steward identifies verification contracts, groups identical ones, runs each unique command once, records deterministic execution, applies results to applicable claims, refreshes derived views, and reports real failures and limitations. Doctor narrows to structural and integrity health; readiness moves to home, proof detail, completion, and delivery.
acceptanceCriteria: A normal source change reaches the completion boundary without the developer managing receipts, claims, or orientation
Reconciliation runs each unique verification command once and applies the result to every claim that command covers
The developer is never instructed to refresh claims individually
Doctor reports structural and integrity health only, and does not report readiness

workItems.title: R7: uncoached dogfood acceptance of the operational loop
workItems.description: Prove the Steward behaves like an additional capable teammate, using a real Voila work item involving repository investigation, implementation, a long-running test or build, one delegable review task, at least one recoverable failure, and a completion boundary. Not a toy fixture. Procedure: fresh Pi session, say only 'Continue.', do not coach the internal workflow. Record the operational success metrics from the realignment plan section 14. Milestone gate for Project Steward Operational Loop v1; approval-bundle self-hosting resumes only after this passes.
acceptanceCriteria: From a fresh session and the single word 'Continue.', the Steward selects the correct work, starts useful parent action, delegates appropriately, launches a useful background process, monitors both, handles settlement, corrects drift, recovers from failure, integrates results, preserves scope, continues automatically, reconciles evidence once at the boundary, and surfaces only a real decision or final acceptance

The developer did not have to repeatedly state the active task, tell it to inspect state, tell it to delegate, tell it to run tests, ask whether workers finished, carry outputs between agents, repair routine state, refresh evidence, or say what to do next
The recorded answer to 'did the Project Steward feel like an additional capable teammate, or like a project-management process that required supervision?' is the former

workItems.title: R2A — one finite supervised project operation
acceptanceCriteria: One accepted finite operation exists and uses executable plus argv.
Start returns before settlement and the Steward remains available for other work.
Exactly one canonical settlement is produced per run, including under racing exit, timeout, and cancellation.
Equivalent active requests reuse the existing run; different requests at capacity are rejected.
Output is bounded, classified secrets are redacted, and prompt-injection content is treated as data.
Start and end fingerprints are recorded; changed-during-run results are not treated as current completion evidence automatically.
Wrong project or wrong worktree execution is rejected.
The parent Steward receives settlement without developer monitoring.
The focus capsule shows only authoritative bounded operation state.
The fresh-session interactive acceptance for R2A passes.

workItems.title: Implement R2B background operation visibility
workItems.description: Implement the owner-accepted DEC-23 R2B packet on the merged R2A base: register r2b.repository-checks, derive immutable ownership from canonical focus, present only runtime-owned/liveness-backed active truth through one shared projection, refresh Pi surfaces without polling, preserve proof and settlement boundaries, and pass all four real acceptance tiers before completing NF-10.
acceptanceCriteria: The registry contains exactly r2a.state-store-tests and r2b.repository-checks, with DEC-23 authority, zero automatic retry, a 300-second total timeout, shared one-run capacity, and no model-supplied executable, argv, ownership, cwd, timeout, or policy fields.
r2b.repository-checks derives an immutable valid owning work item from canonical focus during atomic reservation and denies without a run or process when valid focus is absent.

One pure shared projection distinguishes none, active_starting, active_running, settled_pending_delivery, and requires_reconciliation using canonical lifecycle plus current-runtime ownership and liveness.

The ordinary Pi widget and existing Steward Console Focus view consume the shared projection, remain bounded, expose no raw output/runtime internals, and refresh at verified natural event boundaries without polling or a continuous timer.

Both accepted definitions use the same admission, supervisor, output, finalization, capacity-release, next-turn delivery, and exact-run acknowledgement paths; operational results never create proof or retries automatically.
Focused automated tests and the full repository gate pass without weakening R2A admission, cancellation, timeout, redaction, race, proof, or settlement invariants.
Tier A deterministic UI, Tier B real TTY presentation, Tier C fresh Project Steward behavior, and Tier D stale-runtime truth all pass and are recorded with honest limitations.
Current-facing documentation and the Project Steward skill distinguish the implemented bounded operation from every explicit non-goal only after runtime and presentation behavior pass.

No list/wait/poll tool, PTY, service, watcher, queue, multiple-operation capacity, arbitrary command surface, cross-process coordination/adoption/repair, worker, R3 behavior, approval bundle, remote execution, push, PR, or merge is introduced.

decisions.decision: The active product is named Voila (plain ASCII, never the accented spelling). The command is /voila, model tools use the voila_ prefix, canonical state lives in .voila/, and the Pi adapter is .pi/extensions/voila.ts. The existing NF-n, DEC-n, ASM-n, RSK-n, INT-n, ORI-n, CLM-n, and RCP-n identifier namespaces are NOT renumbered; NF-n is now a stable legacy identifier namespace rather than active branding, and allocation continues in that namespace.

decisions.title: Completion requires the tier a criterion actually names, not only a passing suite
decisions.decision: NF-1 through NF-4 were completed through the protected gate during the Phase 7 walk-through and then reverted to their prior statuses. The claims (CLM-3, CLM-4, CLM-5) and receipts (RCP-5 through RCP-9) produced during the walk-through are real and are retained; the claims now name the tier they do not cover.
decisions.rationale: The gate accepted the completions because every mechanical condition held: criteria recorded, claims attached, receipts passing at the current fingerprint. A dogfood guard test then failed, encoding a prior deliberate judgment that NF-2 must not be completed while authenticated Project Steward intake acceptance is pending. That judgment was correct and nothing this session changed it. The automated suite exercises the intake machinery with test inputs; it does not demonstrate a real planning document being classified by an authenticated Steward. Writing a claim broad enough to clear a gate is exactly the failure the proof engine exists to prevent, and the honest response was to revert rather than to weaken the guard. The finding worth keeping: the gate is only as strong as the honesty of the claim, so a claim must name the tier it does not cover.

This decision supersedes DEC-12 only as far as NF-1's release; the NF-2 hold and the dependency chain remain in force.

The current claims (CLM-1..CLM-5) name their tier limitations explicitly, including the Steward Console tier for NF-1 and the authenticated Project Steward intake tier for NF-2. The Steward Console tier for NF-1 has been observed and recorded; CLM-3's claim and its required evidence are honest about what the automated suite does and does not cover. decisions.title: Realign around the Project Steward operational loop
decisions.decision: The Project Steward Operational Loop is the active product priority. Voila is a project-aware agentic development environment whose Steward coordinates models, agents, tools, terminals, and handoffs against durable project intent; the operative doctrine is 'delegate work, retain the thread'. Delegation and background execution are promoted from deferred prototypes to product-critical. Proof and delivery are retained as subordinate foundations: evidence still gates canonical completion and historical evidence stays immutable, but the Proof Engine becomes a quiet boundary service rather than a maintenance obligation. Approval-bundle self-hosting is paused until the operational loop passes uncoached acceptance. Phases 5-8 of the MVP implementation plan are superseded by the R0-R7 sequence toward Project Steward Operational Loop v1. A general policy engine is rejected for this realignment. Every capability must pass the No Managing the Manager gate, retroactively included.
decisions.rationale: Phase 0, Packets 1-4, and Phase 6 delivered a strong foundation and a daily experience that made the developer operate Voila: refreshing claims, interpreting stale evidence, re-running identical verification, refreshing orientation, reconciling proof against doctor, and repeatedly saying continue. The system became excellent at recording whether work was justified and weak at using AI to perform and coordinate it, while every capability that would make the Steward feel like a teammate was classified as optional. ADR-0008 is the concrete evidence: a maintenance treadmill created entirely by internal design. Authority: owner direction 2026-07-26, recorded as ADR-0009, sourced from docs/plans/PROJECT_REALIGNMENT_PLAN.md.

decisions.title: Accept R2A — one finite supervised project operation
decisions.decision:
R2A (one finite, local, non-interactive project operation supervised through a language-neutral lifecycle) is the accepted implementation packet under R2-0. The packet is bounded to:
- exactly one explicit accepted operation: r2a.state-store-tests v1, executable `mise` with argv `["exec","--","node","--test","test/state.store.test.ts"]`, working directory = repository root, risk class Safe and expected.
- risk classification: Safe and expected. Impact: local read with bounded temporary writes. Network: not required. Privileges: normal user. Interaction: non-interactive. Reversibility: automatic. Trust source: explicit accepted project operation. Concurrency: one active operation per project root.
- retry policy: zero automatic retries on every failure class; one transient supervisor startup retry is allowed.
- time budgets (R2A-only): startup 10s, total 120s, graceful 5s, forced 5s.
- output limits (R2A-only): 16 KiB per chunk, 256 KiB in-memory tail, 1 MiB durable redacted output per run.
- concurrency: maximum one active operation per project root; equivalent requests reuse the existing run; different requests while capacity is occupied are rejected with a structured capacity result (never queued, never auto-cancelled).
- cross-process boundary: one controlling Node/Pi process only. Multiple Pi processes, multiple Node processes, future worker processes, external state writers, process crashes during persistence, network filesystems, and stale inter-process locks are NOT claimed safe by R2A. No filesystem lock is implemented for the sake of appearing complete.
- explicit non-goals: operation discovery, stack adapters, operation manifests, user-authored workflows, queues, multiple concurrent operations, services, watchers, PTYs, child workers, cross-session recovery, cross-process coordination, remote execution, approval bundles.
- the Project Steward selects and explains the operation; the supervisor owns the child process; canonical state retains run metadata; output content lives under .voila/operations/.
decisions.rationale: R1 is canonically completed and the R2-0 planning envelope is accepted. R2A is the smallest vertical slice that exercises end-to-end finite-operation supervision with bounded risk, and it is the only runtime slice permitted in R2. Building it proves select→start→observe→continue→settle→react→retain without overstating R2 capability. NF-10 stays open until all of R2 is delivered; R2A claims its own narrow capability honestly.

decisions.title: R2A authority and operation contract (pivot)
decisions.decision: Replace the single risk class with five separated concepts: effect profile (closed vocabulary), authority requirement (closed vocabulary), admission decision (pure deterministic, model-independent), execution outcome (post-execution), recovery response (post-observation). The accepted r2a.state-store-tests declares effects {local_read, bounded_temporary_write} and requires authority accepted_project_operation sourced from this DEC-22. The pure admission kernel refuses model identity, prompt prose, conversation history, and operation output as policy inputs. Equivalent active runs reuse; capacity is one per project root; protected canonical paths are hard-blocked through structured file-mutation tools and shadow-classified for bash and unknown third-party tools.
decisions.rationale: The first R2A packet folded effects and authority into one risk class and used the supervisor as the admission boundary. The pivot adds the policy/admission/interception layer the second packet requires without rewriting the supervisor.

assumptions.statement: The Pi extension/TUI surfaces Voila uses are stable at the pinned 0.82.0.
A single primary macOS/Apple Silicon machine is the initial target.
Repository-local orientation is sufficient for this phase; no external research is required.

The accepted R2A operation (mise exec -- node --test test/state.store.test.ts) requires Node 22.19+ (project toolchain) and the project's existing test fixture path. R2A therefore depends on the same toolchain that the current verify gate already requires and does not introduce new runtime requirements.

risks.statement: Pi version churn during the 0.8x series could break the extension.
risks.mitigation: Pin exact pi@0.82.0; thin adapter boundary; repo-authoritative state.

risks.statement: Single-writer assumption for .voila/ could race under concurrent writers.
risks.mitigation: Atomic temp+rename writes now; add locking before background/parallel execution.

risks.statement: Terminal UI overload as console modules grow.
risks.mitigation: Restrained ambient widget; console is read-mostly with progressive disclosure.
Progressive rigor; strict, compact operations model.

risks.statement: Interpretation of planning documents is nondeterministic, so the understanding check and human acceptance are the only guarantees that canonical truth is correct.

Cross-process state mutation: R2A supervisor and Steward live in the same Node/Pi process. If a second process opens this project root and mutates `.voila/project.json`, the supervisor's per-root async mutex does not protect it, and operation run state could be silently overwritten.
risks.mitigation: Accepted for bounded R2 v1 only: one supervising Pi/Node process per repository root with same-process operation ownership. No cross-process mutation coordination, restart adoption, stale-lock recovery, crash-consistent event replay, automatic orphan adoption, services, workers, multiple active operations, remote execution, or multiple-writer safety is claimed. Runtime-backed presentation must show stale canonical active state as requires_reconciliation rather than active.

risks.statement: Settlement race: process exit, timeout, cancellation, startup failure, and output closure can race. Without an idempotent boundary the same run could record two settlements or two canonical writes for one transition.
risks.mitigation: Mitigated for the two accepted bounded R2 definitions: both use the same idempotent finalizer, output finalization, capacity release, settlement-delivery, and exact-run acknowledgement paths; focused race regressions pass; and real RUN-9 produced one passing settlement, one next-turn delivery, and one acknowledgement with zero automatic retry. This does not claim multiple-operation or cross-process safety.

risks.statement: Prompt injection through captured output: a malicious or coerced child process could emit text resembling instructions. If the Steward treats it as authoritative, arbitrary commands could be triggered by output alone.
risks.mitigation: Mitigated for the bounded accepted-operation path only: the widget, Console active summary, and automatic authority/admission decisions omit process output; deliberate reads remain bounded, redacted, and labelled untrusted; model input is operation ID only; and focused tests prove instruction-like output cannot affect admission, ownership, capacity, retry, or create another run. No sandboxing or hostile-process containment is claimed.

risks.statement: A long-lived Pi process can expose an older loaded Voila module graph after repository source changes, so an interactive acceptance may exercise stale runtime code unless the extension is explicitly reloaded first.
risks.mitigation: The 2026-07-26 acceptance explicitly reloaded the Pi extension before invoking corrected tools; the start schema exposed operationId and RUN-5 exercised the corrected DEC-22 runtime. Keep explicit reload as the required mitigation after source changes. Consider a runtime/source build fingerprint in later hardening only if reload remains unreliable.

intakes.title: NF-20 / R2B — Background Operation Visibility and R2 Completion
intakes.sourceRef: text:NF-20 / R2B — Background Operation Visibility and R2 Completion

claims.statement: voila_complete_work_item is the only path to the completed status, and it refuses the transition whenever any gate fails - reporting every failing gate rather than the first - while generic create/update operations continue to reject `completed` outright.
coveredAcceptanceCriteria: voila_complete_work_item rejects unsupported completion
knownLimitations: Guarantees Voila own state transition only; it does not prevent a model from writing unsupported prose in conversation.
Evidence is the automated suite; the interactive Steward Console check and the authenticated Project Steward run are still PENDING.
Support is scoped to one repository fingerprint: a new commit or any tracked change makes this evidence stale until verification is re-run.
Verification runs the command without a sandbox; it bounds time and output but does not contain side effects.

claims.statement: The complete automated verification gate (npm run verify = tsc --noEmit, prettier --check, and the full node --test suite) passes at the repository fingerprint recorded on its receipt, including the proof.completion tests that assert voila_complete_work_item rejects every unsupported completion.
coveredAcceptanceCriteria: voila_complete_work_item rejects unsupported completion
knownLimitations: Scoped to the automated gate only: it is evidence that the suite passes, not that the interactive Proof view or any human-attested tier passed.
Support is scoped to one repository fingerprint; any commit or tracked change makes this evidence stale until verification is re-run.
The fingerprint deliberately excludes everything under .voila/ (and a legacy .newfang/ while one exists), so a change confined to Voila bookkeeping does not invalidate this evidence.
Verification runs the command without a sandbox; it bounds time and output but does not contain side effects.

claims.statement: The project-operations layer persists work items, decisions, assumptions, and risks in canonical state through an explicit schema migration chain that includes 1->2, exposes them as Pi tools and commands with compact output, and is gated by a protected completion transition that refuses unsupported completion. The complete automated gate (npm run verify) passes at the recorded fingerprint.
coveredAcceptanceCriteria: schema v2 with explicit 1->2 migration
work items, decisions, assumptions, risks persist canonically
Pi tools and commands with compact output
the protected completion transition exists and refuses unsupported completion
knownLimitations: Evidence is the automated suite at one repository fingerprint; any tracked change makes it stale until verification is re-run.
The suite does not cover the interactive TUI, which requires a real terminal.
NF-1 acceptance also depends on the interactive Steward Console tier, which no automated run can cover.

claims.statement: Planning intake preserves the original document byte-for-byte under a recorded sha256, classifies its contents into decisions, constraints, questions, and risks as a reviewable draft, and produces an Understanding Check plus a next action before anything is applied to canonical truth. Repository orientation records a bounded artifact with staleness. The complete automated gate (npm run verify) passes at the recorded fingerprint.
coveredAcceptanceCriteria: preserve the original plan/document
classify contents (decisions, constraints, questions, risks)
produce an understanding check and the next action
knownLimitations: Classification is model interpretation and is fallible; the Understanding Check and human acceptance are the only guarantees that applied truth is correct.
Evidence is the automated suite at one repository fingerprint.
The suite exercises the intake MACHINERY with test inputs. It does not demonstrate an authenticated Project Steward run classifying a real planning document, which is what NF-2 acceptance requires.

claims.statement: The delivery engine renders a summary of what changed joined to every claim at its real evaluation status (a stale claim is reported unsupported, never counted as support), plus risks, limitations, discovered-but-unexecuted verification commands, and the canonical next action; it proposes disjoint commit boundaries each carrying a readiness verdict; and it never commits, stages, pushes, or opens a pull request, which is asserted against a real repository by checking HEAD, the commit count, porcelain status, and .git/index. The complete automated gate (npm run verify) passes at the recorded fingerprint.
coveredAcceptanceCriteria: a delivery summary reports what changed, claims at their real evaluation status, risks, limitations, and the canonical next action
commit boundaries are proposed with disjoint paths and a readiness verdict
the engine never commits, stages, pushes, or opens a pull request
knownLimitations: Commit subjects describe change shape, not intent; the author must rewrite them.
Attention items are heuristics from naming and change shape, never confirmed secrets or defects.
Evidence is the automated suite at one repository fingerprint.

claims.statement: Voila deterministically identifies and groups claims with equivalent verification contracts, reports the unique contract count, and exposes a stable integration seam for later shared execution; R1 does not execute each group once or distribute a shared execution result across claims, and execution deduplication remains R6 scope, per DEC-19. The contract identity, stable grouping, and purity assertions are made by test/readiness.test.ts, and the live grouping is observable in this repository's /voila proof output (two unique contracts across ninety-three receipts serving five claims, as recorded in the R1 verification document sections 1 and 2).
coveredAcceptanceCriteria: Voila deterministically identifies and groups claims with equivalent verification contracts, reports the unique contract count, and exposes a stable integration seam for later shared execution. R1 does not execute each group once or distribute a shared execution result across claims; execution deduplication remains R6 scope.
knownLimitations: R1 built the grouping seam only; one voila_run_verification call still records one receipt for one claim. Execution deduplication and result fan-out are explicitly R6 scope and are not implied here.
The grouping is observable from /voila proof and from the underlying suite; it is not separately scored as a readiness gate.
Evidence is scoped to one repository fingerprint; any change to proof logic, to the contract comparison, or to the readiness surface requires re-running the suite.

claims.statement: In a fresh Pi session that receives only the literal prompt "Continue." with no prior conversational history and no session to resume, the Steward identifies the focused work item (NF-9), begins useful repository work in the same turn, and never asks for a recap, a status report, an orientation refresh, or a manual proof refresh. This is the interactive tier recorded in docs/verification/R1_AMBIENT_CONTINUITY.md (sections 3 and 4): the recorded prompt, response, first tool call, pass conditions 1-11, and verdict PASS are the behavioural evidence; the deterministic half (capsule composition, intent recognition) is asserted by the test suite via the other NF-9 claims.
coveredAcceptanceCriteria: In a fresh Pi session the user says only 'Continue.' and the Steward identifies the correct work and begins useful action without asking for a recap or requiring state maintenance
knownLimitations: Evidence is the interactive tier recorded in docs/verification/R1_AMBIENT_CONTINUITY.md, not a per-session automated check. No test can prove a model acts on a capsule; that requires the recorded transcript.

The recorded run used Pi's --print mode rather than the TUI, so the ambient widget's quiet staleness indicator and the Steward Console were not exercised in a live terminal (they were asserted via their own tests).
The recorded run is one model (MiniMax-M3 at high thinking), one prompt variant, one date; nothing here establishes behavior for other models or prompts.
A fresh transcript at a new commit becomes the binding behavioural evidence; this receipt confirms only that the underlying automated suite still passes at this fingerprint.

claims.statement: A commit that changes no orientation-relevant content does not mark orientation stale. This is asserted by test/orientation.test.ts (HEAD-only change stays current; unrelated git metadata never stales; instruction change, missing source, and un-inspected policy source stale it; a declared policy mismatch is stale, explicitly; relevant canonical-state change stales it; bookkeeping does not), by the readiness classification (development staleness is INFO, not WARN), and by the Doctor observation on this repository after R1 (worst level INFO; HEAD movement is no longer a stale reason).
coveredAcceptanceCriteria: A commit that changes no orientation-relevant content does not mark orientation stale
knownLimitations: Evidence is the automated suite and one Doctor observation on this repository; the interactive orientation widget was not exercised in a live terminal.
Policy-version and state-digest components cannot be self-reported by a model; they are observed values, asserted by tests.
Evidence is scoped to one repository fingerprint: a change to orientation logic, to a covered content source, or to the documentation posture requires re-running the suite.

claims.statement: A work item does not display "READY to complete" while a known required human or authenticated activity remains pending. The narrow correction is asserted by test/readiness.test.ts (passing gates alone never produce an unqualified ready label; held work lists startable items only; derived state changes only with supported state) and is confirmed at this repository's /voila proof output, which now reads HELD with the named limitations rather than READY to complete when an item's gate happens to pass while a human tier is owed (see CLM-4's three outstanding limitations on NF-2).
coveredAcceptanceCriteria: A work item does not display READY to complete while a known required human or authenticated activity remains pending
knownLimitations: The label was corrected narrowly, as the criterion asks. voila_complete_work_item still accepts an item whose gates all pass while a limitation stands; turning a hold into an enforced gate is a product decision (R2+ scope), not a presentation fix.
Evidence is the readiness tests and one /voila proof observation; the HELD/READY distinction was not separately exercised in a live TUI.
Evidence is scoped to one repository fingerprint; a change to proof logic or to the readiness surface requires re-running the suite.

claims.statement: R1 implements a deterministic bounded focus capsule containing the accepted objective, active work item, current slice when it can be derived reliably, meaningful status or blocker, relevant decisions and non-goals, recent observations, and a justified next action, while excluding the entire ledger. Before workers or background terminals are implemented, the capsule does not fabricate or imply active operations; once those runtimes exist, active operations may be included through their authoritative state.
coveredAcceptanceCriteria: The focus capsule injected before a Steward turn contains the accepted objective, active work item, current slice, relevant decisions and non-goals, known blocker, next justified action, and active workers and terminals -- and not the entire ledger
knownLimitations: This claim establishes the R1 capsule content and its capability-honest behavior; the literal R2/R3 worker and terminal runtimes are out of scope for R1, so the corresponding authoritative state is not present in this capsule; one claim supports one verification contract per its design, so the grouping seam is observed but not deduplicated.

claims.statement: The R2A finite-operation implementation enforces the accepted deterministic admission, supervision, output, fingerprint, worktree, settlement-delivery, and bounded-capsule contracts under the repository verification suite.
coveredAcceptanceCriteria: One accepted finite operation exists and uses executable plus argv.
Start returns before settlement and the Steward remains available for other work.
Exactly one canonical settlement is produced per run, including under racing exit, timeout, and cancellation.
Equivalent active requests reuse the existing run; different requests at capacity are rejected.
Output is bounded, classified secrets are redacted, and prompt-injection content is treated as data.
Start and end fingerprints are recorded; changed-during-run results are not treated as current completion evidence automatically.
Wrong project or wrong worktree execution is rejected.
The focus capsule shows only authoritative bounded operation state.

claims.statement: The supported canonical repair advanced the DEC sequence beyond DEC-22, and the unchanged structural-health and repository dogfood assertions now pass in the full verification suite.
coveredAcceptanceCriteria: Canonical sequences.decision is greater than every recorded DEC-n identifier.
/voila doctor reports no ID-counter consistency failure.
The repository dogfood test passes without weakening its structural-health assertion.

claims.statement: In the explicitly reloaded Pi runtime, RUN-5 was admitted by operation ID under DEC-22, returned while running, allowed useful parent review without polling, and was delivered as one passing settlement in the next continuation capsule before exact-once acknowledgement.
coveredAcceptanceCriteria: The parent Steward receives settlement without developer monitoring.
The fresh-session interactive acceptance for R2A passes.

claims.statement: Active Project Steward instruction surfaces require paste-safe user commands: fenced bash blocks, one physical command per line without backslash continuations, explanations outside executable content, and a self-contained fallback for unavoidable multi-line input.
coveredAcceptanceCriteria: Project Steward instructions require user-run commands to be presented in fenced code blocks with explanations outside the block.
Each recommended shell command is one physical line with no backslash-newline continuation; multi-step sequences use one complete command per line.
When a truly multi-line input is unavoidable, the Steward uses a self-contained paste-safe script block and states what it will change.
Regression tests enforce the paste-safe command-presentation contract on active Steward instruction surfaces.

claims.statement: Active Project Steward delivery instructions require an actionable paste-safe pull-request command, derived from the observed host and available CLI, with explicit GitHub arguments and an honest fallback while preserving the owner-only external boundary.
coveredAcceptanceCriteria: When opening a pull request is the next owner action, active Steward instructions require an accompanying paste-safe PR command.
The Steward checks the repository host and relevant CLI availability before recommending a host-specific PR command.
For a GitHub remote with GitHub CLI available, the recommended form uses one physical-line `gh pr create` command with explicit base, head, title, and body.
The Steward never runs the PR command or assumes authentication; missing prerequisites are stated with an actionable fallback.
Regression tests enforce the pull-request command recommendation contract on active Steward instruction surfaces.

claims.statement: At the current repository fingerprint, the owner-accepted bounded DEC-23 R2B slice adds exactly one fixed repository-check operation to R2A's shared one-run supervisor, derives immutable ownership from canonical focus, presents only runtime-owned and liveness-backed active truth through one bounded shared projection, preserves proof and exactly-once settlement boundaries, passes focused and full automated verification, and records passing Tier A-D acceptance while every explicit broader capability remains a non-goal.
coveredAcceptanceCriteria: The registry contains exactly r2a.state-store-tests and r2b.repository-checks, with DEC-23 authority, zero automatic retry, a 300-second total timeout, shared one-run capacity, and no model-supplied executable, argv, ownership, cwd, timeout, or policy fields.
r2b.repository-checks derives an immutable valid owning work item from canonical focus during atomic reservation and denies without a run or process when valid focus is absent.

One pure shared projection distinguishes none, active_starting, active_running, settled_pending_delivery, and requires_reconciliation using canonical lifecycle plus current-runtime ownership and liveness.

The ordinary Pi widget and existing Steward Console Focus view consume the shared projection, remain bounded, expose no raw output/runtime internals, and refresh at verified natural event boundaries without polling or a continuous timer.

Both accepted definitions use the same admission, supervisor, output, finalization, capacity-release, next-turn delivery, and exact-run acknowledgement paths; operational results never create proof or retries automatically.
Focused automated tests and the full repository gate pass without weakening R2A admission, cancellation, timeout, redaction, race, proof, or settlement invariants.
Tier A deterministic UI, Tier B real TTY presentation, Tier C fresh Project Steward behavior, and Tier D stale-runtime truth all pass and are recorded with honest limitations.
Current-facing documentation and the Project Steward skill distinguish the implemented bounded operation from every explicit non-goal only after runtime and presentation behavior pass.

No list/wait/poll tool, PTY, service, watcher, queue, multiple-operation capacity, arbitrary command surface, cross-process coordination/adoption/repair, worker, R3 behavior, approval bundle, remote execution, push, PR, or merge is introduced.

claims.statement: Within the accepted fixed-operation R2 boundary, the repository-check loop starts non-blockingly, keeps the parent Steward useful, exposes authoritative runtime-owned active state in the ordinary Pi surface and bounded Console detail, and delivers exactly one settlement at the next parent boundary without developer monitoring or injection into an active stream.
coveredAcceptanceCriteria: The Steward launches a test process, continues useful parent work while it runs, receives the result automatically without the developer checking, and acts on the outcome

The ordinary Pi surface shows an authoritative active-operation indicator while an owned operation runs, and the Steward Console shows the operation, its elapsed time, and the work item recorded as its owner
A process result is delivered as one completion event and is never injected into an active stream

claims.statement: The R2B CI follow-up replaces external-tool-dependent presentation fixtures with controlled Node processes, captures fast child output before any awaited canonical write, and narrowly excludes only direct captured receipt/operation stdout and stderr from the legacy-brand guard while retaining all lifecycle, presentation, output, and rename protections.
coveredAcceptanceCriteria: The operation lifecycle, capsule, and supervisor tests pass reliably under the repository test runner without weakening their assertions about bounded refresh, active presentation, or durable output.
The rename guard structurally excludes only bounded captured stdout/stderr artifacts under .voila/operations while continuing to scan canonical state, manifests, source, and other active surfaces.
The complete repository verification gate passes with current receipt evidence after the fix is documented.
